children: Shares of networking chips designer Marvell Technology
fell 8.8% in the afternoon session after the company announced an agreement to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock transaction with an implied enterprise value of $115 billion.

Under the terms of the merger agreement, Lumentum stockholders will receive a fixed exchange ratio of 4.500 shares of the company's common stock for each share of Lumentum owned. The transaction values Lumentum at about $115 billion including debt. The company stated that the combination is intended to establish an artificial intelligence connectivity business. The company hosted an investor webcast and presentation on November 2, 2026, to discuss the details of the agreement.

The move suggests investors could be questioning the financial terms amid growing unease regarding data center expansion economics. The massive all-stock purchase also underscores investor caution around equity dilution and high valuations tied to rapid infrastructure expansion.
What is the market telling us

Marvell Technology’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 64 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 6 days ago when the stock gained 4.1% on the news that major artificial intelligence deals and landmark financing agreements reinforced investor confidence in sustained technological demand as reported by AP News. Market sentiment received a major boost following news that Broadcom obtained $63 billion in bank financing to develop proprietary artificial intelligence chips for Anthropic. The massive commitment, paired with Anthropic filing for an initial public offering and Meta launching an equity offering, signaled to Wall Street that capital expenditure across the technology landscape remains robust.

For chipmakers and hardware designers, these multi-billion-dollar transactions demonstrate that major tech players continue to channel enormous financial resources into specialized infrastructure. Rather than slowing down, corporate appetite for computing power is accelerating, helping lift semiconductor shares and providing essential support to broader equity benchmarks such as the S&P 500.

Marvell Technology is up 99.8% since the beginning of the year, but at $178.60 per share, it is still trading 43.6% below its 52-week high of $316.43 from June 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Marvell Technology’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $2,555.
